Copies of any other testing already performed. DEFER Submit the information to the FAA for a possible Special Issuance Annotate (elements or findings) in Block 60

records.raw_text: Any history of optic neuritis (single or multiple episodes All Submit the following for FAA review: 3. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating ophthalmologist or retinal specialist (preferred) no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam. It must include: • A detailed summary of the history of the condition; • Current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any); • Physical exam findings; • Results of any testing performed; • Diagnosis; • Assessment and plan; • Prognosis; and Follow-up. 2. It must specifically include: • Date treatment completed or if any ongoing treatment or surveillance recommended; • If the condition has resolved; • Underlying cause if identified; • Is the presentation consistent with typical or atypical; • Are there any symptoms, current problems, or remaining abnormalities which could interfere with flight or ATCS duties 3. The Clinical Progress Note must specifically include the best corrected visual acuity for distant and near vision (intermediate - if age 50 or older and First or Second Class). If vision standards are not met, that should be discussed. Include if the visual acuity is expected to change. 4. Visual field testing (30-2 or 24-2) performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam. 5. MRI of the brain and orbits with and without contrast for demyelinating disease. 6. A current, detailed neurological evaluation that meets FAA Specifications for Neurologic Evaluation generated from a clinic visit with the treating neurologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam. 7. Color vision testing must be performed for each eye separately using an FAA acceptable computer-based color vision test, within 90 days prior to the AME exam. Pay particular attention to red desaturation. One-time screening is not sufficient; repeated testing is required, as optic neuritis can affect color vision over time. 8. Copies of any testing performed (visual fields, etc.) DEFER Submit the information to the FAA for a possible Special Issuance Annotate (elements or findings) in Block 60

records.raw_text: 3rd class only All There is NO mandatory recovery period per Public Law 114-190 May 2017, but should be released by the treating physician. After the treating cardiologist and/or transplant surgeon has determined that the condition is stable, obtain the following evaluation(s) and submit them to the FAA for review: 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating cardiologist or transplant surgeon no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam. It should include a summary of the history of the condition or diagnosis; current medications, dosages, and side effects (if any); clinical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment and plan (prognosis); and follow-up. 2. It must specifically include: • A statement regarding functional capacity, modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, and prognosis for incapacitation; • Any evidence of rejection and complete documentation of all rejection history, whether treated or not; • A complete history regarding any infectious process; • A complete history regarding any malignancy; and • Comment on the donor heart status, including any evidence of allograft vasculopathy or any disease state. 3. Labs performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam: • Hemoglobin A1C and • Lipid profile to include total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides. 4. Hospital records to include: • Operative report; • Discharge summary from the physician (NOT the discharge instructions/paperwork given to the patient when leaving the hospital); • Admission (history & physical); • Pathology report (if performed); and • DO NOT submit miscellaneous hospital records such as flowsheets, nursing notes, physician orders, and medication administration records. 5. Coronary Angiogram [cardiac cath] performed no more than 12 months before the AME exam: • Must submit both of the report(s); and • Actual imaging on CD in DICOM format. 6. 24-hour cardiac monitor performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam: ≥ 24-hour cardiac monitor (such as a Holter, Zio Patch, etc.). It should include atrial and ventricular ectopic counts; hourly tabular data to include the longest pause duration and counts of all pauses 2.5 seconds or greater; heart rate (max, min, and average); other histograms and frequency graphs; and the percentage of atrial fibrillation/flutter. 7. Stress Echo. Graded Exercise Stress ECHO (with electrical tracings) no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam in accordance with the enclosed specification sheet. 8. Any other testing already completed or deemed necessary by the treating physician (e.g., myocardial biopsy) DEFER Submit the information to the FAA for a possible Special Issuance. Once all information is received, these cases are reviewed by a FAS Cardiothoracic Surgery consultant

It MUST include a. Complete history detailing any family history of unexplained sudden cardiac death, and b. Any personal history of non-sustained Ventricular Tachycardia, or unexplained syncope. Must include complete measurements and specific attention to maximal LV wall thickness, left atrial size, and maximal LV outflow tract gradient (rest vs. Valsalva). Submit the video resulting from this study on CD- ROM in DICOM compatible format. 3. Cardiac monitor. 72 hours minimum performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam
